learning_outcomes.text: Acquire a general understanding of mathematics and natural sciences and develop analytical thinking habits.
Develop knowledge in fundamental topics related to Electrical-Electronics Engineering.
Gain the ability to identify, define, formulate, and solve engineering problems, and to select and apply appropriate analysis and modeling methods for this purpose.
Acquire the ability and skill to analyze and design systems.
Translate theoretical knowledge into practice through laboratory and project work.
Effectively use current software and hardware.
Gain the ability to work in a team and individually.
Gain the ability to communicate orally and in writing. Effectively use a foreign language in professional life.
Awareness of the necessity of lifelong learning; ability to access information, monitor developments in science and technology, and continuously renew oneself.
Gain professional responsibility and ethical awareness.

syllabus_topics: Smart meters and advanced metering infrastructure
Smart grids in generation, transmission, and distribution systems.
Renewable Energy Sources and Energy Storage
Smart Source: Integration of Renewable & Distributed Generation
Smart grid applications in the world
Smart grid applications in the world
Smart Infrastructure, Smart Charging, Smart Devices
Smart Consumers, Smart Demand, Smart Metering, Demand-Response
State Estimation in Smart Power Grids
assessment_rules: Midterm and final exam dates are not specified in the 14-week course schedule. Midterm and final exam dates are determined by the decision of the University Senate and are held on the dates specified in the academic calendar.
